scope: Independent topic review only; no prose, media or publication approval
scenario: Read the complete captured Microsoft announcement, including rollout text and footnotes, then assess the proposed beginner angle.

assessment.reader_demand: Qualitative inference: PC users benefit from knowing where AI processing occurs, what file/network access is permitted, and whether the feature is available on their own machine. Search volume and future traffic are unknown.
assessment.evidence: Direct Microsoft announcement supports local/cloud routing, containment/identity/manageability, MXC GA, Copilot+ future rollout and device/market/silicon limitations. Promotional superiority claims are not independent comparative evidence.
assessment.usefulness: Practical three-part decision guide: processing location; allowed data/actions; availability and device conditions.
assessment.durability: Conceptual distinctions remain useful after announcement; rollout dates and requirements require later updates.
assessment.differentiation: Windows execution/data boundaries and device rollout differ from post219 response UI and post218 game creation.
assessment.freshness: Oct7 date is within36h at the supplied selection instant under publisher US-calendar or UTC-calendar interpretation. Exact publication time/timezone unknown; not a fully measured exact age.
assessment.risk: Conflating MXC GA with universal Copilot availability; treating local context as guaranteed local-only processing; treating containment as perfect safety or every action as separately confirmed; implying a new PC or RTX Spark is required for all features.

required_boundaries: Describe local/cloud as a hybrid architecture; local file access and local model inference are separate concepts. Do not promise fully offline use, no outbound data, or universal cost savings.

MXC is announced generally available on Windows11; individual safeguards still require Windows Update and have staged availability by device, market and silicon. GA does not imply all agents/features are already supported everywhere.
Copilot hybrid capabilities on Copilot+ PCs are expected to begin rolling out in coming months. Do not describe them as already available to every current Windows PC.
Local context/actions are permission-based according to Microsoft. Do not invent a specific permission dialog, per-action confirmation guarantee, scope or user flow without another source.

If mentioned, GitHub HydraFusion Windows integration is experimental preview later in October; new Search actions first roll out to Insider experimental channel; Search/Copilot integration is opt-in in selected markets later this year. Keep those timelines distinct.
Frame suggested first steps as checking Windows/device eligibility, release information and permission scope; no firsthand-use claims or guaranteed current click-by-click procedure.
Do not reproduce Microsoft promotional performance/safety superiority as established fact. Omit hardware benchmark details unless the exact tests and qualifications are essential.
Exact publication instant, measured search volume, velocity and traffic forecast remain unknown.
